Review-round-1 continuation completed. I continued numbering from E023, conducted targeted searches across all reviewed chapters, and added the following evidence units. No scores or score ranges were assigned.

## New evidence register entries

| ID | Evidence and precise locator | Profile / disposition | Lens mappings |

| E024 | Philippine delegation stated at the TPNW meeting on 21–23 June 2022 that the Philippines was a State Party, constitutionally prohibited nuclear weapons on its territory, adhered to the Southeast Asia Nuclear-Weapon-Free Zone, supported IAEA safeguards/CTBT compatibility, and pledged verification, universalization, dialogue, and disarmament measures. [UNODA statement, pp. 1–2](https://documents.unoda.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Philippines.pdf) | UN treaty record, high for formal position; transition-period official conduct, not implementation proof; final evidence | 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.4, 1B.6, 1B.8, 1B.10 |

[2022 Human Rights Report, pp. 1–5](https://fln.dk/media/jpja3grg/fili105.pdf) | Government report, medium-high; distinguishes stated restraint, investigations, continuing abuses, and weak remedy; final evidence with attribution caveats | 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.4, 3B.5, 3B.6, 3B.9, 3B.10; 8B.6, 8B.8 |

## Chapter disposition

1B improved materially but remains bounded. E024 establishes a direct Philippine 2022 disarmament and nuclear-risk position; E025 supplies formal inherited safeguards; E026 limits exposure; E027 adds target-period cyber-risk capacity evidence. No evidence was found of nuclear weapons, nuclear threats, nuclear command operations, proliferation, or a nuclear crisis involving Marcos. Practical safeguards and implementation remain unresolved. The chapter is not saturated on command safety or high-risk cyber/biological/AI governance.

2B gained direct target-period evidence through E031 and the rejected E032 lead. The record now supports diplomacy, defensive framing, rules-based maritime conduct, and crisis communication. Civilian harm, proxy support, arms-recipient conduct, insurgency peace talks, and accountability for security operations remain insufficiently documented. The failed PNA fetch is a retrieval blocker for that specific claim, not evidence of absence.

3B gained a materially useful ruler-attributed accountability and security-policy item in E028–E029. The evidence distinguishes Marcos’s stated rehabilitation/due-process shift from continuing killings, investigations, and weak prosecutions. E030 strengthens the inherited/pre-accession boundary. Remaining gaps are security appointments/orders, vulnerable-group protection, later-2022 remedies, and evidence of actual correction or tolerance.

4B gained independent corroboration of the inherited transition environment through E030 and direct post-accession accountability conduct through E028. The main unresolved issue is whether Marcos personally directed campaign disinformation or inherited media restrictions, plus later-2022 surveillance, protest, court, legislative, and succession conduct.

5B and 6B gained E033 as contrary shock/distribution context. It does not independently verify government performance. Plans, budgets, outcomes, and external shocks remain separable; implementation audits, household/regional outcomes, service quality, and distribution remain open gaps.

7B gained E028 as a direct ruler-specific accountability decision, but it is not sufficient to establish a broader personal-integrity pattern. E015 remains appointment context, and E021 remains non-admissible country-level corruption context. Asset declarations, conflicts, procurement, personal benefit, truthfulness, and correction evidence remain missing. E022 remains rejected.

8B gained E027, E028, E029, E031, and E033. These add evidence of cybersecurity-capacity planning, accountability strategy, security-policy execution, diplomatic implementation, and shock response. Independent delivery audits, coordination failures, adaptation, personnel replacement, and durable multi-program outcomes remain unresolved.

## Search and source-diversity audit

- Nuclear searches covered UNODA/TPNW, IAEA treaty and safeguards records, SIPRI inventory, IAEA civil-nuclear material, and cyber-risk assessments.
- Security searches covered specialist regional analysis, official maritime reporting, inherited conflict records, and contrary escalation leads.
- Human-rights searches covered Amnesty, CPJ, the U.S. human-rights report, and CHR-related leads.
- Economic and social searches covered World Bank, PIDS, DOF/DBM, and official poverty/inflation reporting.
- No recent-news filters were used.
- E018 and E023 were not duplicated; E024–E026 are distinct treaty, safeguards, and inventory claims.
- E032 was not counted because the underlying page could not be fetched precisely.
- No client-matrix material was used.
